title: Asian-session range breakout at the European open on 15m, 1R target, flat by 12:00 UTC
rule_summary: Chart 15m, closed bars, UTC clock; signal at a bar close, filled at the next open. Every day, weekends included. ASIAN RANGE: AH = highest high and AL = lowest low of the 28 bars opening 00:00 to 06:45 UTC. DAILY FILTER: ATR(14) with Wilder smoothing, built from closed UTC daily candles (informative 1d, only completed days, last value = yesterday). The day is armed only if 0.25 <= (AH-AL)/ATR14 <= 0.80. ENTRY WINDOW: bars opening 07:00 to 09:45 UTC. If, inside the window, a bar closes below AL before any bar closes above AH, there is no trade that day (the first break is downward). Otherwise, at the first bar close above AH, buy at the next open. One trade per day at most. STOP: AL, checked intrabar. TARGET: entry + (entry - AL), i.e. 1R, as a limit. TIME EXIT: if neither is hit, sell at the open of the 12:00 UTC bar. The longest hold is about 5 hours.
mechanism: Per Quantpedia's 'Periodicity in Cryptocurrencies' (arXiv 2109.12142), crypto volatility bottoms near 05:00 UTC, Binance illiquidity peaks in the East-Asian night, and activity steps up around 08:00 UTC. So the 00-07 UTC range forms in thin trading, and European desks bring fresh directional flow. Stop orders of range traders sit just beyond AH, and triggering them fuels the push. The width filter skips dead days and days already exhausted. The 1R target is at least 0.25 x daily ATR (about 1% or more here), well above the 0.45% conservative round trip. This is FX-session practice carried over to crypto, where the 07-08 UTC liquidity arrival is documented.
